items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: And then I had a fellow called Snow Fisher.

ctx.x: Now, these two fellows could HANDLE on any part of the sporting world and they could control anything that went on down there. But Ben Allen was getting old now, and he was tired of this business, so he turned the place over to Charley Reynolds. But Charley Reynolds was a younger fellow and he had his gambling going there and everything, so he wanted a good show. He figured that being at Kentucky and Arctic Avenue, that was the hub of the black belt. Where everybody, both the people who were good and the people…

See, so, he said, 'Sam, you can bring a band in here.' I had about, let's see, I had five, six musicians at that time. He said, 'Come on in here and find me some girls that are good entertainers. And a man to go along with them.' So, that's when I picked up the two Ethels and another girl named Izzy Ringgold, which was a very good dancer and singer. In fact, she outsung most of the girls at that time. She was very good. And then I had a fellow called Snow Fisher.

Well, we worked all the summer. And, of course, being in the heart of town, there wasn't no laying off. You had to keep the music going all the time. Often, I'd keep the music going.
